rationale: Records the repeat of fixed experiment 3b4f2310a3bf43a492eea0cfedd79dd0-experiment: every decisive operand of the boundary and default-configuration pairs came back identical, so the replay-completion account cites its second execution and drops the single-run wording for those two pairs.

interpretations.rationale: Extension note: this successor adds the second execution of the fixed experiment (receipt 9039d268ffc24fa085efc75de7dc4fb2) as reproducibility evidence for the boundary and default-configuration pairs; sources, knowledge uses, conclusion and the other executions are unchanged, and the counterevidence and limitation that described those pairs as single-run are updated accordingly. Precision note: the entry-based batch figures recorded by the earlier receipts equal the delivered counts there, and the receipts' own operands show why. In receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f event 16 the prefix ends at log index 9002 with staged commit index 9001, so the replayed range holds the bootstrap configuration entry, one no-op and 8999 commands, that is 9000 tuples, and ceil(9000/64) = 141, the figure the receipt records for that case. Receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 records 1501 and 3001 replayed entries with 94 and 188 batches at MaxAppendEntries 16, and the same counting gives 1500 and 3000 tuples, ceil(1500/16) = 94 and ceil(3000/16) = 188. The two counts diverge only where the replayed range ends inside a batch in a way that adds a no-op, which is what the boundary receipt's 2049-entry range with 128 delivered batches shows. Reproducibility: the fixed experiment that produced the boundary and default-configuration pairs was executed a second time from its retained inputs in a clean copy (receipt 9039d268ffc24fa085efc75de7dc4fb2), and every decisive operand came back identical - the 2049-entry range again held 2048 tuples in 128 batches and returned in 0ms (events 30, 31, 32), the 2050-entry range again held 2049 tuples in 129 batches and did not return with three stack samples (events 33, 34, 35), and the default-configuration prefix again recorded staged commit index 12001 with snapshot index 0 and no snapshots listed against a bound of 8192, with the replay-enabled restart not returning and the control returning (events 36 to 41). The only differing operand was the control's return latency, 3ms in the first execution and 1ms in the repeat. A citation check of this account against the retained observations found no other discrepancy. Correction note: this successor extends the previous account of this question with the default-configuration receipt; sources, the earlier executions, knowledge uses, conclusions and limitations are otherwise unchanged, and the counterevidence item that recorded default-cadence reachability as unmeasured is replaced by the measured statement. Correction note: this successor differs from the previous account of this question only in two transcribed numbers and their attribution; the flag-off control of receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f returned in 1ms and the same control of receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 returned in 5ms, as those receipts record, and the earlier account had them swapped. Everything else - sources, executions, knowledge uses, counterevidence, limitations and joint history - is unchanged. Mechanism. With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs set, NewRaft reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs with it before starting any background goroutine (api.go:723-754). processLogs walks the committed range and appends a commit tuple only for entries prepareLog accepts - commands and barriers always, configuration entries when protocolVersion > 2, and nothing for no-op or deprecated peer entries - flushing a batch whenever the batch reaches config.MaxAppendEntries and delivering it through a select whose only other case is shutdownCh (raft.go:1296-1364 with prepareLog at raft.go:1364-1391). fsmMutateCh is created with capacity 128 (api.go:560) and its only consumer runFSM is started by api.go:636-638 after the replay returns, so a replay needing more than 128 delivered batches waits for a consumer that cannot exist until the blocked call finishes, with no timeout. Block and bound. Receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f restarts a single-voter prefix holding 9001 committed entries above an absent snapshot (event 16, 141 delivered batches at MaxAppendEntries 64); the flag-on restart admitted by event 17 did not return within 8000ms (event 18, stack naming processLogs at raft.go:1346 called from restoreFromCommittedLogs at api.go:753 called from NewRaft) while the flag-off restart of the same shape returned in 1ms (event 21) and became leader (event 22); receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 reproduces both, with its own flag-off control returning in 5ms (its event 21) and adds a pair at MaxAppendEntries 16 where 1501 replayed entries (94 batches) returned in 0ms (event 25) and 3001 entries (188 batches) did not (event 29). Receipt 8a710c75d1814aafad5d24b536998539 then places the boundary exactly: at MaxAppendEntries 16 one prefix ends at staged commit index 2049, whose replayed range contains 2048 entries that become commit tuples, that is 128 delivered batches (event 31), and NewRaft returned in 0ms (event 32, comparison holds); the other ends at 2050 with 2049 tuples, that is 129 delivered batches (event 34), and NewRaft did not return within 8000ms (event 35, comparison violated, three stack mentions naming the replay frames). The pair differs only in one replayed command, so the bound is the 128-slot channel measured in delivered batches, and any count derived from the log's index range is an upper bound: the entry-based figure for the returning case also reads 129 batches (event 31), because the range includes entries that produce no tuple. Default configuration. Receipt 0cb30b6bf8874d479b83653bd4e6c553 builds two further single-voter prefixes with Config.DefaultConfig values left untouched: event 36 records SnapshotThreshold 8192, MaxAppendEntries 64, SnapshotInterval 120s, 12000 applied commands, staged commit index 12001, snapshot index 0, no snapshots listed, and a committed range of 12001 entries above the snapshot against the bound of 128*64 = 8192 tuples; the flag-on restart did not return within 8000ms with four stack samples naming the replay frames (event 38, comparison violated), while the flag-off control returned in 3ms (event 41, comparison holds). The trigger therefore needs no tuning of threshold or batch size: the automatic snapshot loop wakes on a randomized timeout of up to SnapshotInterval (snapshot.go:71-95), so a node that commits faster than that cadence carries a range above the bound into its restart. Availability. Receipt ebb3bb9fa26547f790129eea909d1d5a builds three voters at MaxAppendEntries 16, commits 3000 commands through a leader that is not A (event 9), restarts A in a goroutine, and observes the same non-return (event 10). With the replay on the group kept committing with two members live and lost the ability after one further member was stopped (event 11: commit_while_two_live_ok true, commit_after_stop_ok false, error 'leadership lost while committing log'), while with the replay off the same stop left the pair {leader, A} live and the command succeeded (events 13, 14). The corrected unit matters for the recorded gaps: the three correction gaps ask about the premise change, and the receipt answers them substantively - the returning case's entry-based figure was 129 batches while only 128 were delivered, so counts derived from a log index range are upper bounds. Defect account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft cannot complete startup whenever the replay delivers more than 128 batches, that is more than 128*MaxAppendEntries entries that become commit tuples above the restored snapshot index; at the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 that is 8192 tuples, and it is proportionally smaller for any smaller legal value, as measured at 16 (2048 tuples returning, 2049 blocking). The failure is a startup liveness failure: the node never begins participating, so a single-voter group stays down, a larger group runs with proportionally less fault tolerance, and one further stop was enough to make a three-voter group unable to commit. Pending operations the leader had accepted are answered with ErrLeadershipLost once it steps down (raft.go:508-528).

knowledge.assertion: Batches are counted in commit tuples, so no-op and deprecated peer entries consume no batch slot and configuration entries do so only above protocol version 2.
fsmMutateCh has capacity 128 and its consumer runFSM starts only after the startup replay returns.
The replay range above the snapshot sets the number of tuples to deliver, and the automatic snapshot cadence is the only bound on that range in a default deployment.
With the flag on, lastApplied is set to the persisted commit index before the replay, so the replay range spans the committed log above the snapshot.
The tracked latest configuration feeds quorumSize and the vote-admission checks, which is why a member that never starts is simply absent from every future majority.

counterevidence: The block itself is evidenced by non-return within an 8000ms window plus a stack sample per blocked case (events 18, 29, 10 and 35). The permanence argument does not rest on those samples: the source shows no timeout, a single consumer started only after the blocked call returns, and an escape requiring an object the caller has not received. The flag-off controls return promptly in each receipt: 1ms at event 21 of receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f, 5ms at event 21 and 0ms at event 25 of receipt e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00, and 0ms at event 13 of receipt ebb3bb9fa26547f790129eea909d1d5a.

The boundary pair has now been executed twice from the same fixed inputs in separate clean copies with identical operands (receipts 8a710c75d1814aafad5d24b536998539 and 9039d268ffc24fa085efc75de7dc4fb2), but its delivered-tuple count is computed by the harness scanning the replayed range with the same type rule prepareLog uses rather than read from an internal counter; the behaviour straddles the boundary by one replayed command, and the tuple figure is an inspectable operand rather than the decisive predicate.

The default-configuration case is a burst: the harness applies commands as fast as the in-memory stack allows and no automatic snapshot had fired at restart (event 36: snapshot index 0, no snapshots listed). It reproduced identically in the second execution of the same fixed experiment (receipt 9039d268ffc24fa085efc75de7dc4fb2, events 36 to 41). It shows that default settings do not keep the range below the bound during a burst, not how long a node typically stays above it, and the other cases that raised SnapshotThreshold made the condition permanent rather than momentary.

The availability case contains a deliberate second stop, so what it shows is the loss of the group's fault-tolerance margin rather than an outage in an untouched cluster; the control with the replay disabled performs the same stop and still commits, which is what attributes the loss to the member that did not return.

In the flag-on availability case the surviving leader's command failed with 'leadership lost while committing log', which is the leader stepping down and failing its pending operations rather than a defect of its own; the same apply succeeded while two members were live (event 11) and after the same stop in the control (event 14).

The blocked NewRaft call is abandoned in a separate goroutine so the tests can complete; that is a harness choice, not a repair, and no harness observes the process-level consequence of a caller that waits forever.
limitations: All cases run in one process over in-memory transports and a test commit-tracking store; no production store, no process-level restart and no disk fault are exercised, and the confined goroutine is the only trace of the real caller's hang.

The availability case uses one prefix shape, one batch size (16) and one extra stop; the boundary case uses one batch size and one run per side; observation windows are 8000ms for restarts and 3000ms for the applies.

Schedule variation is unevenly covered: the original 9000-entry pair appears in two receipts, the boundary pair and the default-configuration pair have each been executed twice from the same fixed inputs with identical operands, while the bound pair and the availability pair remain single-run, and each blocked state is still sampled once per execution.
The bound's dependence on the caller-side store is assumed rather than verified: the replay range comes from the stored commit index, whose durability contract belongs to the LogStore implementation.
interpretations.joint_history: All four receipts are executions of fixed experiments for this investigation on the same captured source revision, in separate workspaces with no shared mutable state, and their harnesses share the same initialization: an in-memory commit-tracking log store, a single-voter bootstrap for the first three, RestoreCommittedLogs enabled on the prefix, and the restart in a separate goroutine with an 8000ms window. Receipt 3d04552f58e548b0ae089192392b564f and its revision e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 use one harness whose cases differ only in Config.MaxAppendEntries and the committed range, and e82594cc274340f0a961608cda519e00 re-runs the original 9000-entry pair unchanged. Receipt ebb3bb9fa26547f790129eea909d1d5a uses a three-voter harness at the same MaxAppendEntries 16 and observes the same block. Receipt 8a710c75d1814aafad5d24b536998539 uses the first harness's prefix construction with targets chosen from an earlier construction run of the same case and places the replay on both sides of the channel capacity. The blocked state in every receipt is corroborated by a stack sample naming the replay frames, and no receipt depends on another's runtime state. Receipt 9039d268ffc24fa085efc75de7dc4fb2 is not a separate producer at all: it is the same fixed experiment as receipt 0cb30b6bf8874d479b83653bd4e6c553 executed a second time in a fresh clean copy, which is why its events carry the same names and indices. Receipt 0cb30b6bf8874d479b83653bd4e6c553 uses the same single-voter prefix construction with Config.DefaultConfig left in place for the snapshot settings, so its operands (staged commit index, snapshot index, replay batches) are directly comparable with the earlier receipts' fields of the same names.
